title: Beyond Indexing and Citation Counts: A Context-Responsive Framework for Evaluating Scholarly Publications in African Higher Education
content: Dominant publication-assessment practices in higher education often treat journal indexing, citation counts, download statistics, journal impact factors, and publication in internationally prestigious venues as convenient proxies for scholarly quality and impact. These indicators can support research evaluation when they are used cautiously, transparently, and in combination with expert judgement. Yet they become problematic when they operate as context-blind gatekeepers for faculty promotion, career progression, and university ranking. This problem is especially acute in African higher education, where unequal research funding, limited article processing charge support, fragile scholarly publishing infrastructures, language hierarchies, and uneven representation in global bibliographic databases shape the visibility of knowledge before evaluators judge its value. This article develops a context-responsive publication-evaluation framework for African universities using secondary data, integrative literature review, documentary analysis, conceptual synthesis, and normative framework development. Drawing on responsible research assessment, decolonial theory, epistemic justice, open science, bibliometrics, African higher education studies, and university-ranking methodologies, the article distinguishes publication quality from publication visibility, scholarly influence from social usefulness, and citation attention from public value. It proposes a multidimensional framework that retains rigorous standards of originality, method, ethics, peer review, and transparency while incorporating contextual relevance, policy influence, pedagogical contribution, professional uptake, accessibility, regional inclusivity, and long-term transformative potential. The framework offers universities, promotion committees, quality assurance bodies, and ranking agencies a defensible route toward fairer evaluation without abandoning scholarly rigor.
